Hildegard 0.1.3 is a pre-alpha. It fixes upgrades from 0.1.1, reaches Hildegard from your other devices and from chatbots, and works with the local models you already run.

## Install

- **macOS and Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh`
- **Windows (PowerShell):** `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex`
- **Desktop app:** pick your system's download below, or from [dbaney.com/hildegard](https://dbaney.com/hildegard/).

## Fixed

- **Upgrading from 0.1.1** no longer makes an installed model read as not installed, on the GPU computer and on every device paired with it. Hildegard now fetches the 343 MB safety check on its own when an installed model is missing it.

## New

- **Hildegard's tools from anywhere.** AI apps on your other devices reach Hildegard over Tailscale with a key: `hildegard host key "<name>"`, then `hildegard connect <app> --remote <link>`. Keys stay in the keychain, never in an app's config. claude.ai and ChatGPT can sign in to Hildegard with OAuth, and every call runs with that person's own permissions.
- **Your local models.** Hildegard finds Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, MLX, Jan, KoboldCpp and the Local AI gateway running on this computer (`hildegard llm`). `hildegard llm direct "<idea>"` lets one of them direct a film.
- **Stricter provider rules.** Only the owner can run Claude on the owner's account or key, invited people included. claude.ai, ChatGPT and Copilot plan addresses and plan tokens are refused as model endpoints, since those plans may only be used in their own apps.
- **LTX's terms** in Hildegard now say what its license asks: label LTX videos as machine-generated wherever you share them.

## Known limits

- Macs don't render on their own GPU yet. Pair a Mac with a computer that has an NVIDIA or AMD GPU
  (`hildegard choir join`).
- The Windows and macOS apps aren't code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask you to confirm the first launch.
- Hildegard Link, the encrypted relay for reaching Hildegard without Tailscale, is a prototype and not switched on yet.
- LTX models follow Lightricks' license: free under $10M yearly revenue, and not for products that compete with
  Lightricks. Wan 2.2 is Apache-2.0.
